title: Diffusion Engineers Ltd - 544264 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,415.74 million (+38.08% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income was INR206.89 million (+39.96%), at a 14.61% margin. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR4,066.28 million (+21.28%) with PAT of INR504.1 million (+39.87%). Standalone growth was weaker: Q4 revenue +12.18% and Q4 PAT down 3.05%, which management attributed to capacity constraints in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering running at about 85-90% utilisation. Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

segments.name: Welding consumables (products)
segments.commentary: Management cited roughly 30% of revenue; under 3% (said 2-3%) of the business is conventional, with the rest special hard-facing and repair electrodes. Wires line at 85-90% utilisation; new wire line expected July 2026.

segments.name: Wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering
segments.commentary: Cited at roughly 30% of revenue combined with heavy engineering; running at 85-90% utilisation, and expected to grow faster than consumables. Roller-press rolls, steel mill rollers and VRM rollers are cited as growth areas; first VRM order won.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.name: Railways (developmental)
segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.name: Defence (Tejorup Sunmay Systems)
segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 20%, supported by capacity additions, order inflows and higher-margin engineered products.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise by about 80-100 basis points, aided by operating leverage and cost consolidation; gross margin may come under pressure from raw material volatility.
Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

Capex of about INR100 crores from IPO proceeds (INR70 crores for wear part/plate/heavy engineering, INR30 crores for electrode and slitting facility) is expected to support INR800-900 crores revenue; no additional capex planned for INR650 crores.
Debtor days targeted at 80-85 for FY27 and inventory days at 60-65; FY26 debtor days were 98 and inventory days 66.
International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.
Current utilisation: wires about 85-90%; wear plates and heavy engineering about 85-90%. Management expects utilisation to fall to roughly 50-60% once new shop floors are live.
New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: When will railway and defence businesses contribute meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway developmental orders take 6-9 months to execute, with substantial revenue from next year after approved-vendor listing. Tejorup defence revenue is not expected in FY26 or significantly in FY27, pending prototype approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue contribution from new products such as steel mill rollers and VRM rollers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing confidentiality; said steel mill roller revenue was significant last year, a first VRM order has been won, and shredder spare parts are under development.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (tungsten, cobalt, nickel) on fixed-price contracts; gross margin pressure in FY27 with a lag in passing through costs.
Standalone profitability: Q4 standalone PAT fell 3.05% YoY despite revenue growth, and standalone growth depends on Unit 4 commissioning on schedule by end of Q1 2027.
Receivable days at 98 in FY26 with heavy-engineering payment cycles of 75-90 days; management's 80-85 target needs to be met.
Quarterly concentration: Q4 is seasonally large, and management expects Q4 to remain the biggest quarter.
Tejorup defence and railway developmental businesses carry lower initial margins and long gestation periods.
Management's stated 20%+ FY27 growth and 80-100 bps margin expansion are to be tracked against Q1 FY27 results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity additions, with management stating a preference for prudent guidance and an intent to over-deliver. More cautious and specific on raw material pass-through and receivables, where answers relied on contract structure and time lags. Declined to quantify new product revenue, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: Our intention is always to sort of, you know, over perform the commit, over the commitment that we are or the indication that we are giving.
So, we believe in, you know, being, you know, being sort of prudent in terms of giving indication.
So, whatever needs immediate deliveries are fixed price contracts. And contracts which are staggered in terms of deliveries will have price friction clauses built into them.
I don't think and I don't foresee any revenue coming in from Tejorup in this financial year.
Sir, we can connect offline if needed because this is confidential data and it's sensitive to our business.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of more than 20% (midpoint 20%), backed by Unit 4 capacity starting Q1 FY27 and an order book of about INR200 crore (up from INR100 crore a year earlier, 80-90% to execute in FY27), though standalone Q4 growth was only 12% and no specific revenue bridge was given.
